text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Swedish/U.S. drugs major Pharmacia & Upjohn PNU.ST has appointed Fred Hassan as its new chief executive office (CEO). Chairman Jan Ekberg had acted as CEO after John Zabriskie suddenly stepped down in January.
- A softer crown is expected to help boost export companies profits. A partial effect of the weaker currency will probably be seen in the second quarter and the full effect in the third.
- Sweden is preparing for its prisons to receive war criminals from former Yugoslavia but will require that prisoners have some connection to the country.
- American Fred Hassan will become the new chief executive of Swedish/U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn.
- As of next year the Swedish customs might again be allowed to seize alcohol if a committee's proposal goes through.

- No other sector is growing as quickly in Sweden as suppliers and operators for the Internet and information technology. In only one year the number of companies operating in the sector has grown to 500 from 150 and turnover now totals around 11 billion crowns.

- Car safety equipment maker Autoliv's result will improve next year following the group's merger with a unit of U.S. Morton after the new company carries out a reorganisation of its plants. The most drastic changes will take place at operations in Germany, The Netherlands, the United States and Japan while Swedish operations will not be affected, interviews with company management reveal.
- Finnish telecoms group Nokia is a true success story on the Stockholm Stock Exchange. Turnover of the shares in the first four months of the year already matches that during all of 1996.
